name: Additions to Daniel: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
sourceNote: Translated from the Greek of Daniel 3:24–90 in the version of Theodotion, as printed in H. B. Swete, *The Old Testament in Greek according to the Septuagint*, vol. 3 (1899; public domain), which gives on facing pages the Old Greek (Septuagint proper, preserved in full only in the Chigi manuscript 88 and the Syro-Hexapla, with Papyrus 967 reported in later editions) and the Theodotion text that replaced it in church use. Differences of substance in the Old Greek are given in the notes. These verses are part of the Greek and Latin book of Daniel, standing between Dan 3:23 and 3:24 of the Hebrew-Aramaic text; in the Latin Vulgate and Catholic Bibles they are numbered Daniel 3:24–90, and the verse numbers here (1–68) follow NRSV and do not correspond one-for-one with those. They include the Prayer of Azariah (vv. 1–22), a prose narrative (vv. 23–27), and the Song of the Three (vv. 28–68), whose second part (vv. 35–68, the Benedicite) has long been sung in Christian worship. No Semitic text survives; many scholars hold that the prayer and song were composed in Hebrew, perhaps in the 2nd century BC. Azariah, Hananiah and Mishael are the Hebrew names of Abednego, Shadrach and Meshach (Dan 1:6–7). These additions are received as Scripture by Catholic and Orthodox churches; Protestant churches place them among the Apocrypha. Greek *kyrios* is rendered “Lord” and *theos* “God.” Measures are given in US units with the original and metric values in the notes; dates are given as BC/AD. Readings not checked directly against the manuscripts are cited “as reported.” Brenton’s English (1844), which translates the Old Greek, was consulted only as a check and not copied. CJT draft.

verses.text: And they walked about in the midst of the flame, singing hymns to God and blessing the Lord.{a}
And Azariah stood up and prayed thus, and opening his mouth in the midst of the fire he said:

Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers,
and praiseworthy, and your name is glorified to the ages.

For you are righteous in all that you have done to us,
and all your works are true, and your ways are straight,
and all your judgments are truth.

You have carried out true judgments
in everything you have brought down upon us
and upon our ancestors’ holy city, Jerusalem;
for with truth and justice you brought all this
upon us because of our sins.

nor did we keep them or do as you commanded us,
so that it might go well with us.

And all that you brought upon us,
and everything that you did to us,
you did in true judgment.

Do not hand us over to the end, for your name’s sake,
and do not annul your covenant,

and do not take your mercy away from us,
for the sake of Abraham, the one beloved by you,
and for the sake of Isaac your servant
and Israel your holy one,

For, Master, we have been made fewer than every nation
and are brought low today in all the earth because of our sins.
But with a crushed soul and a humbled spirit may we be received,{e}

And now we follow you with all our heart,
we revere you and look for your face.
Do not let us be disgraced,

but treat us with your kindness
and with your overflowing compassion.

And rescue us according to your wonders,
and give glory to your name, Lord.

and let them know that you alone are Lord God,
and glorious over the whole inhabited world.
And the king’s servants who had thrown them in did not stop heating the furnace with naphtha and pitch and tow and brushwood.
And the flame poured out above the furnace to about seventy-three feet;{g}
and it spread out and burned up those of the Chaldeans whom it found around the furnace.
But the angel of the Lord came down together with those around Azariah into the furnace and shook the flame of the fire out of the furnace,
and made the middle of the furnace as if a wind of dew were whistling through it; and the fire did not touch them at all, nor give them pain, nor trouble them.
Then the three, as from one mouth, sang a hymn and glorified and blessed God in the furnace, saying:

Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers,
and praiseworthy and exalted above all to the ages;

and blessed is the holy name of your glory,
and greatly praised and exalted above all to all the ages.

Blessed are you in the temple of your holy glory,
and hymned above all and glorified above all to the ages.{h}

Blessed are you who look upon the abysses,
seated on the cherubim,
and praiseworthy and exalted above all to the ages.

Blessed are you on the throne of your kingship,
and hymned above all and exalted above all to the ages.

Blessed are you in the firmament of heaven,
and hymned and glorified to the ages.

Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord;{i}
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you heavens;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you angels of the Lord;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, all you waters above the heaven;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, all you powers;{j}
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, sun and moon;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you stars of heaven;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, every shower and dew;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, all you winds;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, fire and burning heat;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, chill and scorching;{k}
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, dews and snowfalls;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, nights and days;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, light and darkness;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, frost and cold;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, hoarfrosts and snows;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, lightnings and clouds;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Let the earth bless the Lord;
let it hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, mountains and hills;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, all things that spring up on the earth;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you springs;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, seas and rivers;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you sea monsters{l} and all things that move in the waters;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, all you birds of heaven;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you wild beasts and all you cattle;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you sons of human beings;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, Israel;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you priests of the Lord;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you slaves of the Lord;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you spirits and souls of the righteous;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Bless the Lord, you who are holy and lowly in heart;
hymn him and exalt him above all to the ages.

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is kind,
for his mercy is to the ages.{n}

notes.text: Inserted after Dan 3:23. The Old Greek opens instead: “So Hananiah and Azariah and Mishael prayed and sang hymns to the Lord when the king commanded that they be thrown into the furnace.”
Nebuchadnezzar, or, in the author’s own day, perhaps Antiochus IV Epiphanes (175–164 BC).
Compare Hos 3:4. The line fits the time when the temple worship was halted (167–164 BC; 1 Macc 1:41–64), as many hold.

The Greek line “and be fully accomplished behind you” (ekteleisai opisthen sou) is obscure; the Old Greek, as reported, reads differently here, and some correct the text to “and may we wholly follow you.”
Greek “forty-nine cubits,” about 22 m; a cubit is about 18 inches (45 cm).
The order of verses 31–34 differs somewhat between Theodotion and the Old Greek, as reported.
Verses 35–68 are the canticle known from its Latin opening as the Benedicite. The refrain renders hymneite kai hyperypsoute auton eis tous aiōnas.
The sequence of the elements named in verses 42–51 differs between Theodotion and the Old Greek, as reported.
Greek kētē, the great creatures of the sea, including whales.
The Greek and Latin text of Daniel continues at 3:24 of the Hebrew-Aramaic (“Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished…”), numbered Dan 3:91 in the Vulgate.
